newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China has contingency fund for HK stocks - paper.
newsitem.headline: China has contingency fund for HK stocks - paper.

text.p: China has set up a contingency fund to bail out Hong Kong's stock market if it experiences a sharp drop after the colony reverts to China next year, the Beijing-backed Ta Kung Po newspaper reported on Tuesday.

Zheng Wantong, a Chinese Communisty Party official, was quoted as telling Hong Kong stockbrokers in Beijing that China had set up the contingency fund and made other plans to ensure the stability of Hong Kong's stock market after 1997.
Zheng is a deputy head of the Chinese United Front Work Department, a party organ which works to galvanise support for Beijing among other Chinese political groups.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
Although the impending handover has affected neither investment nor the stock market in Hong Kong, some fear political uncertainty could dampen the investment climate in the future.
The fund is managed by Chinese Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji, the newspaper reported.
Zheng was quoted as saying China would take appropriate steps if the market's stability was threatened, but gave no details.
